Answer: B
Reason: Scimitar syndrome is a congenital condition typically associated with right lung hypoplasia (often involving the middle and lower lobes, but can affect the upper lobe or be generalized) and anomalous pulmonary venous return. The images show a small right hemithorax with mediastinal shift to the right (dextroposition), which is caused by volume loss in the right lung, consistent with aplasia or hypoplasia of a lobe (option B).
